title: THE MATCH-CUT OPEN
cites: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_ACT1_OPENING_VISION_7_19_26.md - THE MATCH-CUT OPEN (7/19, Paolo, locked shape) and OPENING SEQUENCE CRYSTALLIZED beat 1 (NIGHT RAID)
note: AUTHORED FROM THE LOCKED SHAPE. Every beat traces to a line of his 7/19 addendum, quoted in `why`. ALWAYS MAKE AN ATTEMPT (Paolo 8/11, LOCKED): every line below is a REAL attempt at the words, written as if it ships, and tagged draft:true so he can find and edit every one. The previous version shipped these beats SILENT under the old empty-contents reading, and his own diagnosis was that the blank page is what stopped the quests. STRUCTURE IS STILL HIS: who dies, who lives, the casualties, the dials -- none of that is decided here. LENGTHENED 8/11 after Paolo watched v1 and said "it was short": +3 lines (father at the table, the older sibling before the cut, the father's second half after it) and +2 holds. Every added line carries its catalogue citations per the same day's DIALOGUE ALWAYS REFERS TO THE CATALOGUE ruling. No new DECISION is taken: nobody new is placed, nobody dies, nothing is named that he reserved.

beats.why: 'The game opens on a PRE-APOCALYPSE family dinner... the family whole, the world intact, a warm happy moment at the table.'
the framing must be IDENTICAL either side of the cut or the match-cut does not read as the same table.
'You are a CHILD, the family whole.'
'the family whole' at the pre-collapse table. He is the one who wakes you ten years later, so the player must have seen him whole first.
'the family whole' at the pre-collapse table. The cold open ends saving her, so she is established here before she is at risk.
the older sibling is the SAME GENDER as the player (7/19 RESOLVED); the surface picks which body from creation.

the one taken on night one sits at this table first, so the empty chair later has a memory attached. 'MOTIF SEED: the sibling's EMPTY CHAIR persists at family meals' is [PENDING] and is NOT built here.

beats.speaker: mother
beats.text: Sit down, both of you. It's getting cold.
beats.why: 'a warm happy moment at the table' (7/19). ATTEMPT (8/11 rule): the most ordinary sentence in the world, on purpose -- the cut has to take something SMALL and real, not a speech. 'Both of you' quietly establishes two siblings before one of them is gone. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: THE BLINDSIDE (mundane -> devastating)
study.applied: the corpus is explicit that the setup's LIGHTNESS is what makes the drop land, so the opening line of the game is deliberately the least remarkable sentence in the house. A portentous first line spends the match-cut before the match-cut happens.

study.title: THE HOUSE'S INTERIOR IS ONE ROOM DEEP
study.applied: that study's named failure is a siege-home with no domestic texture, where 'the family exists in two character models and a closet'. Food going cold and a mother counting heads IS the domestic texture, bought in one sentence before the same house gets besieged.

beats.speaker: sibling_lost
beats.text: I'm not eating the green ones.
beats.why: ATTEMPT (8/11 rule): the sibling who is taken on night one gets one line, and it is a child being a child about vegetables. Nothing portentous. The whole weight of this scene depends on her being unremarkable here. WHICH sibling is lost is HIS ruling (7/19 leaning) -- this speaks whoever the surface casts. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: ATTACHMENT FROM MUNDANE INTIMACY
study.applied: the only bond the player will ever get with this sibling has to form in one line, and the corpus says the bond forms through quiet ordinary emotionally-available moments, the everyday IS the attachment, not melodrama. So she gets vegetables, not a goodbye.

study.title: FORESHADOW-IN-HINDSIGHT
study.applied: a line that only lands LATER, so the scene plays differently in memory than in the moment. Petty refusal of a vegetable is the last ordinary thing she says, and the player only learns that afterwards, which is the entire mechanism that study describes.

study.title: THE HOUSE'S INTERIOR IS ONE ROOM DEEP
study.applied: 'no child's drawings' is one of the three absences that study names by hand. This is the child's drawing, in audio, and it costs six words.

beats.speaker: mother
beats.text: {sibling_lost}. Green ones too. We do this every night.
beats.why: ATTEMPT (8/11) + backlog 0sc's 8/13 amendment, which asks for the name and one quirk surfaced BEFORE the fight. It rides the line above rather than adding a new idea: his existing "I'm not eating the green ones" already IS the quirk, and one tired sentence from the mother turns it into a ten-year-old family bit AND lands the name. "We do this every night" is the whole job -- it tells you this has a history without a word of exposition. NOTHING NEW IS DECIDED: nobody is placed who was not already at this table, and the name is a draft in `cast`. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: ATTACHMENT FROM MUNDANE INTIMACY
study.applied: the beat above already cites this and already got it right: the bond forms through quiet ordinary moments, so she gets vegetables and not a goodbye. What it did not have was a NAME, and an unnamed person is a role. The mother saying it while telling her to eat is the cheapest possible way to land one, because that is how a family actually uses a name.

study.title: THE BLINDSIDE (mundane -> devastating)
study.applied: "the setup's lightness makes the drop land." This is the setup, and it is deliberately the lightest line in the scene: a tired mother losing the same argument about vegetables she loses every night. Nothing here is allowed to be portentous or the drop stops working.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: They're saying the water district's hiring again. I'll go down Monday.
beats.why: ATTEMPT (8/11 rule). PAOLO 8/11 ON v1: "it was short". The pre-collapse half was two lines long, so the warmth had no time to become a place. This is the father whole, ten years before he is the man in the dark: a guy with a Monday and a job to go ask about. It also puts the ECONOMY in the first thirty seconds without a word of exposition, which is the game's own subject. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: TRANSACTION-CARRIES-EMOTION
study.applied: the corpus is blunt about it: do not open with 'here's a sad story', open with the errand and let the weight sneak in under it. The first thing this family talks about is WORK, which is the instrumental frame, and every ounce of grief the scene later earns arrives underneath it.

study.title: CARTOONY SURFACE, REAL DRAMA UNDER
study.applied: a warm surface makes the drama land HARDER. A man cheerful about a hiring notice is the warmest thing in the scene and it is thirty seconds from being the last normal Monday anybody in this room gets.

beats.speaker: sibling_older
beats.text: Can I take the truck Saturday? I'll put gas in it, I swear.
beats.why: ATTEMPT (8/11 rule): the older sibling gets a line BEFORE the cut so the voice that speaks after it is one you have already heard, which is the only reason the after-line lands. A teenager negotiating for the car is the most ordinary sentence a teenager has ever said. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: AMBIENT BANTER AS CHARACTERIZATION
study.applied: the corpus calls overheard, ordinary talk the cheapest and highest-impact characterisation there is, and names it solo-dev gold. Nobody in this exchange is telling the player anything; they are just a family at a table, and that is what makes them one.

study.title: W4 (fair-play seeding — MANDATORY
study.applied: seed relentlessly from the start so the later beat is inevitable-in-hindsight. He asks for the truck and gas; both of those become currency in about ten years, and neither is remarked on here.

beats.why: the warmth has to land before it is taken, or the cut costs nothing.

'Then a blink / match-cut: the SAME table, ~10 years later, now in a dingy post-apocalypse house, you are 20-something. The single cut shows the entire apocalypse without a word.' THIS BEAT IS THE WHOLE OPENING.
same place, ten years on. What the world was, what it became.
'you are 20-something' - same seat, same framing, different person.

*** THE PERSON TAKEN TONIGHT WAS NOT IN THE ROOM TONIGHT. *** The 7/19 shape is explicit that she does not die at the table -- "the death happens during the raid, away from it, in motion, in the house" -- which means she is alive AT this table, minutes before, and the scene simply never staged her. The player's entire acquaintance with her was one line as a child ten years ago. This is the hole backlog 0sc's 8/13 amendment names: attachment before the death was a WATCHED match-cut and nothing else. Staging her costs no decision -- she is already established at this table and already ruled to die away from it.
'the 10-YEAR ANNIVERSARY OF THE FOURTH OF JULY... the one night you see recreational FIREWORKS'. It also sets up the raid: 'you can't always tell a firework from a muzzle flash'.

PAOLO 8/11 ON v1: "it was short". The after-room got two beats before somebody spoke. A room that has been lived in for ten years needs to be LOOKED at before it is explained, and silence is the only thing that makes a boarded window mean anything.

beats.speaker: sibling_older
beats.text: Same chair. Ten years and you still take the same chair.
beats.why: ATTEMPT (8/11 rule): the first line after the cut has to make the audience LOOK at the table again and understand what happened without narration. It also names the empty seat without naming it. Sits on the [PENDING] EMPTY CHAIR motif seed WITHOUT building it. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: THE MUNDANE HOOK -> COSMIC DREAD
study.applied: the ordinary frame makes the reveal land harder. The first thing said after ten years of apocalypse is about SEATING, so the player's own eye does the reveal instead of a narrator doing it for them.

study.title: EXPOSITION-HEAVY / LORE-DUMP LATE
study.applied: that study's failure is unloading the world's truth in big talky chunks, and its lesson is DRIP-FEED. The collapse therefore gets zero words here. The line points at the furniture and lets the player count the chairs.

study.title: THE HAUNTED SPACE
study.applied: the shack tells its story environmentally without exposition. Here the TABLE is the haunted space: same frame, same seats, one of them empty, and nobody explains it.

beats.speaker: sibling_lost
beats.why: THE SAME BIT, TEN YEARS AND ONE APOCALYPSE LATER, and it is the second of three. The match-cut's whole job is showing what survived and what did not; this is a small human thing that survived, said by the one person who will not survive the night. It is funny for exactly as long as it takes to become unbearable. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: MANUFACTURED ATTACHMENT, THEN FORCED BETRAYAL (Companion Cube)
study.applied: the corpus is blunt that attachment is ENGINEERED so its destruction hurts, and the tone research measured our version of the failure: before this, the player met the person who dies tonight for one line, as a child, ten years earlier. She was not in the room on the night she is taken. Now she is, and the last thing she does is be annoying about food.

study.title: FORESHADOW-IN-HINDSIGHT
study.applied: "a line that only lands LATER; the quest plays differently in memory than in the moment." In the moment this is a joke about a bad dinner. After the raid it is the last ordinary thing she ever said, and the player heard it ninety seconds before it stopped being available.

beats.speaker: sibling_older
beats.text: There's nothing in it. Eat it.
beats.why: ATTEMPT (8/11). The surviving sibling's only warmth toward the one who is about to be taken, and it is deliberately not warm on the surface -- flat, unbothered, the way you talk to somebody you assume will be at the table tomorrow. THE STRAIGHT MAN (dialogue craft card 4): the bit needs a normal reaction to bounce off or it is a person being quirky at nobody. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: ATTACHMENT FROM MUNDANE INTIMACY
study.applied: the older sibling is the one who survives and carries the whole game, so the player has to see the two of them be siblings ONCE. Not a speech: the flat unbothered correction you only give somebody you have eaten with every night of your life.

study.title: THE PERMANENT PRE-GAME LOSS
study.applied: "even heroes lose people" is the instant-stakes move, and it only works if the people were people. This line exists so the surviving sibling is not merely a companion slot but somebody who had a sister an hour ago.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: Up. Now. Don't turn the light on.
beats.why: 'Your FATHER wakes you: bandits/raiders are attacking the home.' ATTEMPT (8/11 rule): low and flat, not shouted -- a man who has thought about this night before it came. The third sentence does the work: it tells you they are close enough to see a window, without a word of exposition. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: NODE SURVIVOR_COMFORT
study.applied: that node's banked rule is REMOVE THE ALIBI VERB: the game withholds the sentence that would let the pressure out. The father is given no comfort verb. He does not say it will be okay and he does not explain what is outside, because either one is a pressure valve on the scene the tutorial is about to be.

study.title: DREAD, NOT JUMPSCARES
study.applied: glimpse, withhold, imply, never show the monster. The raiders are not named, counted, or described. 'Don't turn the light on' tells you they are close enough to see a window, and that is the only fact the player gets.

study.title: W7 (one crystallizing line
study.applied: the ports master asks for ONE line that crystallizes the theme and implicates. Seven words set every rule of the night: move now, obey, and light is what kills you. The rest of Act 1 runs on those three.

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: Back door. Behind me, and don't run until I say run.
beats.why: ATTEMPT (8/11 rule). PAOLO 8/11 ON v1: "it was short". The father had one line and then the scene ended, so the tutorial arrived from nowhere. This is the second half of the same breath: it hands the player the shape of the fight before the fight, which is what a tutorial's first line is for. Still no explanation and still no comfort. EDIT FREELY.

study.title: ROLE-ASSIGNMENT AS CHARACTER-KNOWLEDGE
study.applied: competence-casting: a man who knows his people puts each one where they belong. He assigns a door, an order of march and a trigger word in eleven words, which tells you he has thought about this night before it came without one line of him saying so.

study.title: NODE SURVIVOR_COMFORT
study.applied: REMOVE THE ALIBI VERB, held for a second line. The easiest sentence to write here is a reassurance, and the corpus's whole finding is that the reassurance is a pressure valve. He gives instructions instead, and the player is never told it will be alright because nobody in the room knows that.

beats.why: 'The tutorial IS the family-defense fight. You learn the (fun) combat by fending them off room to room.' NAMED TO COMBAT'S OWN CONTRACT (8/11, tools/bohemia_alpha_cold_open_patch.py): they expose startColdOpen(onEnd) with encounterId 'cold_open'. My first version said 'family_defense' and the two halves WOULD NOT HAVE MET -- two lanes building complementary pieces that never connect is this repo's most expensive recurring bug, so the gate now checks the name against theirs instead of trusting it.

'It ends when you save your MOTHER from a raider. The assault is INFERRED, never shown or dwelt on.' The saving beat and the sibling's death are COMBAT's and his to author; the scene returns control here rather than dramatising something he has not ruled.
